chunks: Muʿāwiyah ibn Maysarah narrated from al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام that he said:
"It is not appropriate for the Imam, if he breaks his wudu (ablution), to appoint anyone except one who was present at the iqamah. If he appoints one who has missed a rakʿah..."
For indeed, ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān narrated from him عليه السلام that he said:
"When he completes the prayer with them, he should gesture to them to the right and left so that they may depart; then he should complete what he missed of his salat (prayer)."

key_terms.أَحْدَثَ: entered a state requiring renewal of wudu (ablution)
key_terms.الْإِقَامَةَ: the call announcing the commencement of the congregational salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the prayer leader in congregational salat (prayer)
key_terms.فَلْيَنْصَرِفُوا: so that they may depart after completion
key_terms.مَسْبُوقًا: a follower who joined late and missed part of the prayer

ai.seo_question: Who may replace the Imam in congregational prayer if the Imam breaks his wudu?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about replacing the Imam in congregational salat (prayer) if the Imam breaks his wudu (ablution). It indicates that the replacement should be someone who was present from the iqamah, and if a latecomer who missed part of the prayer leads the congregation to completion, he then completes his own missed portion afterward.
